children: Building products company Boise Cascade Company
will be reporting results this Monday after market close. Here’s what to expect.

Boise Cascade beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $1.83 billion, up 5.2% year on year. It was a stunning quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates and a solid beat of analysts’ EBITDA estimates.
Is Boise Cascade a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Boise Cascade’s revenue to grow 5.5% year on year, a reversal from the 2.7% decrease it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Boise Cascade has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at Boise Cascade’s peers in the industrial distributors segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Richardson Electronics delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 18.9%, beating analysts’ expectations by 10.1%, and WESCO reported revenues up 16.6%, topping estimates by 5.1%. Richardson Electronics’s stock price was unchanged after the resultswhile WESCO was down 1.2%.

In the last twelve months or so, the market has shifted its attention from one area of macro importance to the next (AI disintermediation and AI capex spending to geopolitical conflict, rates, and whether the economy is on solid footing or not). While some of the industrial distributors stocks have shown solid performance in this choppy environment, the group has generally underperformed, with share prices down 3.2% on average over the last month. Boise Cascade is up 5.1% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $91 (compared to the current share price of $78.80).
